Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- FOMC tone remains hawkish (rate liftoff, balance-sheet runoff) amid strong labor markets and Ukraine-related uncertainty.
- SLOOS signals near-term resilience on the business side: banks eased standards for C&I; reported stronger loan demand across large, middle-market, and small firms; and expect improvement in business lending, including non-syndicated C&I and CRE (construction and land development). This offsets some downside risk.
- However, SLOOS also points to consumer/housing headwinds: banks expect deterioration in household credit quality (credit cards, auto, nonconforming jumbo mortgages) and reported weaker demand for residential real estate and GSE mortgages. With interest rates expected to rise, consumer-sensitive sectors face more pressure.
Net: still cautious-hawkish, but SLOOS business-credit strength nudges tone closer to neutral, while consumer/housing fragility keeps a slight negative tilt.
